Before you sign a 787 dollar car payment, see why your neighbour ends up 24,000 dollars ahead.
Theo and Max earn exactly the same.
Theo buys used, and pays about 580.
Theo invests the difference, every month, until the loan is paid.
Meanwhile, Max's new car loses about half its value in five years.
Six years later, both loans are done, and both men own a car.
But Theo also has about 17,000 dollars.
Ten years on, at a typical 7 percent a year, it's around 24,000.
Same paycheck. The difference was one monthly payment.
